title: Psychiatric (co-)diagnoses in critically ill patients. A retrospective cohort analysis with a control group matched for age, sex, diagnosis, and severity of illness.
summary:
Approximately 19% of ICU patients have a history of mental disorders. Patients admitted to the ICU with a history of mental disorders have poorer outcomes in terms of quality of life. In addition, psychiatric disorders contribute to the complexity of critical illness and lead to higher rates of mechanical ventilation, organ failure and mortality.
The FOCUS study is intended to help identify particularly vulnerable patient groups or characteristics among patients with a history of psychiatric illness in order to draw conclusions about their risk of complications and/or mortality. To this end, a comparison will be made with a control group of intensive care patients without a history of psychiatric illness.

interventions.name:
Patients with :
- Treatment in one of the surgical intensive care units of the University Hospital Ulm and
- existing psychiatric illness prior to intensive care treatment. Psychiatric disorders are defined as those listed in Chapter V "Mental and Behavioral Disorders" (F00-F99).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Treatment in one of the surgical intensive care units during the study period (01.01.2013 - 29.02.2024).
Presence of psychiatric illness prior to ICU treatment. Psychiatric disorders are defined as those listed in Chapter V "Mental and Behavioral Disorders" (F00-F99).
Exclusion criteria:
Psychiatric disorder acquired during intensive care treatment (postoperative delirium, treatment-related stress disorder).
Diagnosis: F17.2 - Mental and Behavioral Disorder Caused by Tobacco (Tobacco dependence as the sole diagnosis is not considered a separate psychiatric disorder).
